hypothesis: A one-season conditional residual table is noisy, while an input feature made from same-season target encoding is train/inference-inconsistent. Retain only the conservative magnitude of exact-C residual effects whose sign agrees in both of the two latest completed outer-time folds.

relationship_to_prior_work.v4_robust_group_effects: That screen tuned one immediately previous-season flat group table around the published M3 anchor. This recipe uses exact-C outer-fold residuals, a fixed hierarchy, two-season sign consensus, and the V5 honest-anchor contract.
relationship_to_prior_work.v5_temporal_stable_joint_direct: That model appended same-season leave-one-out target encodings during training and previous-season encodings during validation. This recipe never uses target encoding as a direct model feature; it transfers only completed outer-fold residual effects.
relationship_to_prior_work.public_v18_record: Uses only the publicly described pitcher-by-batter-hand and pitcher-by-pressure-by-batter-hand structure; no model artifact, external data, or leaderboard-derived weight is used.

effect_recipe.route: R only; F remains the exact-C prediction
effect_recipe.source_residual: control_success minus exact-C outer-time prediction, centered by source-season R mean
effect_recipe.consensus: if both source effects are known and have the same nonzero sign, use that sign times min(abs(effect_Y-2), abs(effect_Y-1)); otherwise zero
effect_recipe.candidate: (1-gamma)*exact_C + gamma*component on R; exact_C on F

validation.selection: maximize minimum 2022 full gain across exact-C and both honest anchors, then exact-C R gain, then smaller gamma
validation.on_fail: close without reading 2024 for this recipe
validation.on_pass: write an immutable 2024 recipe lock before opening 2024
